thread_text:
maria: FYI ACME reported streaming sessions cutting out mid-response when going through their corporate proxy. They see partial SSE payloads then the connection closes. Root session: 1859012345
acme-sre: We reproduced locally — the client gets a few `data:` events, then the connection drops with a `502` from our proxy (we use an old F5 appliance). No errors from app tier.
maria: Can you paste a minimal repro curl please? Also which deployment: dedicated or private?
acme-sre: Private (on-prem control plane + VPC peering). Repro: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://private.redwood.acme/streams/v1/generate?model=gpt-small"` It prints some SSE lines then boom.
amos: @maria adding eng-runtime. Sounds like chunk boundary / MTU or proxy buffering. Does the proxy rewrite chunked responses or buffer until a threshold?
acme-sre: The proxy advertises a 1500 MTU to our VPC. The proxy does some response buffering and enforces a max header/body size. Logs show `upstream prematurely closed connection`.
lee: Can we see the raw server logs for that session? Any `write: broken pipe` or socket errors?
anika: I pulled the dedicated host logs for the time window — no OOMs. Runtime shows successful token flushes to stdout, then the downstream connection reset by peer. Example trace from runtime:```
[I] 2026-03-10T15:12:11.123Z stream session started id=abcd-1234
[I] 2026-03-10T15:12:12.045Z chunk flushed bytes=512 id=abcd-1234
[I] 2026-03-10T15:12:12.460Z chunk flushed bytes=480 id=abcd-1234
[W] 2026-03-10T15:12:12.872Z write error: connection reset by peer id=abcd-1234
```
maria: So runtime is flushing small chunks and the proxy closes. Could be MTU or proxy deciding the session is idle because no TCP keepalive or long pauses between flushes. ACME said they have large client-side timeouts too.
amos: Two hypotheses: 1) Proxy buffers until a full TCP segment then resets on chunked boundary (buggy behavior), 2) Proxy enforces a maximum chunk/response buffering window and kills long-poll SSE.
lee: Quick repro I ask customer to try: reduce flush gap by setting runtime option `sse_chunk_target_bytes=128` to send more frequent tiny chunks (workaround) OR enable continuous keepalive pings from client.
acme-sre: We tried toggling client keepalive — still hit the reset. But when we run a small local nginx reverse proxy that passes through chunked transfer without buffering, SSE works fine.
anika: That strongly points at their corporate proxy (F5) doing response aggregation or TCP reassembly. Can they disable response buffering or set `tcp-mss`?
maria: @acme-sre can you capture a tcpdump on the ingress for the failing session? We want to see packet sizes and TCP RST timing.
acme-sre: Attached a short pcap excerpt (sent privately). Observed RST from proxy immediately after a chunk with size 1200 bytes, seq jumps, no FIN.
amos: That looks like MTU + proxy fragmentation interaction. The chunk crosses the MTU boundary and the proxy mishandles the reassembled segment and issues RST. Two mitigation paths: 1) Lower egress MSS on our side (reduce segment size) so chunk sizes stay below 1400 bytes, 2) Have them update proxy config (disable response buffering/aggregation).
lee: For short-term support, we can implement a server-side workaround: configure runtime to limit per-chunk payload so we never emit a chunk larger than N bytes. Do we have a config knob?
anika: We have `streaming.max_chunk_bytes` in private config default 4096. We can set it to 1024 per-customer via tenant config. That will produce more, smaller SSE events but avoids crossing MTU.
maria: Action items: 1) Ask ACME to try the nginx passthrough test (they did and it worked), 2) Apply temporary `streaming.max_chunk_bytes=1024` to their tenant on private runtime, 3) Capture tcpdump once more after change.
acme-sre: Applying smaller chunk limit now in staging... reproduction still intermittently fails but frequency dropped. We'll re-run capture.
amos: Also add a note in support KB: recommended settings when customers front-facing corpproxy/big-FWs — set chunk limit to <= (MTU - 200) and enable application keepalive.
lee: Long term we should detect repeated upstream RSTs and fallback to a non-streaming JSON poll mode (send final output as single response) — at least as an automatic fallback for private customers.
maria: Agreed. We'll coordinate with product for graceful fallback flag. @amos can you prepare a quick patch to tenant config to expose `max_chunk_bytes` UI plus automatic fallback if X RSTs within Y sessions?
amos: Yup I'll prototype. Also adding a check to the deployment checklist: run `mtu-probe.sh` from ingress to corpproxy to detect likely MTU/fragmentation issues. Example probe:```
# mtu-probe.sh
for m in 1500 1400 1300 1200; do
  ping -M do -s $((m-28)) -c 3 corpproxy.example || echo "mtu $m failed"
done
```
maria: nice. ACME — once you confirm post-change capture we can either close or escalate to infra for their F5 config. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Incident ticket created: SUP-2026-2043 linked to this thread.
acme-sre: Post-change capture attached — no RSTs seen in the new window, looks stable. Thank you.
maria: Closing after 24h stable. If anything reoccurs, re-open and add tcpdump + proxy config snippet. :white_check_mark:
